SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these can cause child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Kind neighbours
   B. Poverty and harmful beliefs
   C. Good schools
   D. Enough food

2. Which law forbids child labour and FGM in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing forbids it
   B. Only school rules
   C. Only a poster
   D. The law of Kenya, including the Constitution and the Children Act

3. Which of these is a correct body safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Keep it a secret if someone does
   B. Say nothing
   C. Anyone can touch them
   D. No one should touch your private parts

4. Which is a responsibility of a child? (1 mark)
   A. Skip school
   B. Steal
   C. Bully others
   D. Respect others and study hard

5. What should you do if someone makes you feel unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   B. Stay silent
   C. Keep it a secret
   D. Fight

6. What is an election? (1 mark)
   A. A school holiday
   B. A prayer
   C. A process where people vote to choose leaders
   D. A kind of game

7. A candidate gives sweets for votes. What is this? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating
   B. Fair campaigning
   C. Democracy
   D. Kindness

8. What is a candidate? (1 mark)
   A. A voter
   B. A teacher
   C. A person who stands to be elected
   D. A cleaner

9. What does a class representative do? (1 mark)
   A. Cooks food
   B. Brings the ideas and complaints of classmates to the meeting
   C. Punishes pupils
   D. Teaches lessons

10. What should a Children's Government NOT do? (1 mark)
   A. Welcome visitors
   B. Represent pupils
   C. Organise clean-up days
   D. Punish other pupils by itself

11. What is an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. A sports match
   B. A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   C. A game
   D. A kind of food

12. Which quality means not boasting or looking down on others? (1 mark)
   A. Humility
   B. Greed
   C. Pride
   D. Anger

13. What is a community? (1 mark)
   A. A group of people who live in the same area and share things
   B. A kind of animal
   C. A type of crop
   D. A school subject

14. Who is a leader? (1 mark)
   A. A person who breaks rules
   B. A machine
   C. A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   D. A stranger

15. What is a clan? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of road
   B. A school
   C. A market
   D. A large family group with a common ancestor

16. What does the county executive do? (1 mark)
   A. Carries out the laws and runs county services
   B. Trains police
   C. Makes national laws
   D. Prints money

17. Who helps the governor? (1 mark)
   A. The driver
   B. The pupil
   C. The deputy governor
   D. The cook

18. How many county governments are there in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 47
   B. 37
   C. 57
   D. 27

19. What does the county assembly do? (1 mark)
   A. Cooks meals
   B. Makes county laws and approves the budget
   C. Drives buses
   D. Trains footballers

20. What is a duty of an MCA? (1 mark)
   A. Command the army
   B. Represent the people of the ward in the assembly
   C. Run national hospitals
   D. Issue passports

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe the steps in a fair class election. (4 marks)

22. Name four members of a typical Children's Government. (4 marks)

23. Name four forms of child abuse. (4 marks)

24. Explain what devolution means. (2 marks)

25. Explain three elements of democracy and give an example of each in school. (5 marks)

26. State three functions of the Children's Government. (3 marks)

27. Explain what a child should do if someone makes them feel unsafe. (3 marks)

28. Explain the difference between the governor and the president. (3 marks)

29. Who is the patron of a Children's Government? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Poverty and harmful beliefs
   Poverty and harmful beliefs are causes.

2. D — The law of Kenya, including the Constitution and the Children Act
   Kenyan law protects children.

3. D — No one should touch your private parts
   Your body belongs to you.

4. D — Respect others and study hard
   Rights come with responsibilities.

5. A — Say no, go to a safe place and tell a trusted adult
   Telling an adult is right.

6. C — A process where people vote to choose leaders
   Elections choose leaders.

7. A — Cheating
   Buying votes is unfair.

8. C — A person who stands to be elected
   Candidates ask for votes.

9. B — Brings the ideas and complaints of classmates to the meeting
   Class representatives speak for their classmates.

10. D — Punish other pupils by itself
   Only teachers decide on discipline.

11. B — A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   An agenda gives the order of business.

12. A — Humility
   Humble leaders are modest.

13. A — A group of people who live in the same area and share things
   People in a community share a market, a school or customs.

14. C — A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   Leaders guide and help.

15. D — A large family group with a common ancestor
   A clan traces its origin to one ancestor.

16. A — Carries out the laws and runs county services
   The executive runs the county.

17. C — The deputy governor
   The deputy governor supports the governor.

18. A — 47
   There are 47 counties, each with its own government.

19. B — Makes county laws and approves the budget
   The assembly makes laws and approves the budget.

20. B — Represent the people of the ward in the assembly
   MCAs represent their wards.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Announce, nominate candidates, campaign, vote, count votes in public, and declare the winner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group of two correct steps.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: President, deputy president, Speaker, and class representatives. Accept cabinet members or secretary.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each member.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Early and forced marriage, female genital mutilation, child labour and child trafficking. Accept slavery, sexual abuse, abuse of children with special needs or unsafe transport.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each form.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means sharing power and resources between the national government and county governments.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing power, 1 mark for national and county.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Equality: one vote each. Freedom of expression: giving opinions in class. Majority rule: choosing a game by most votes. Award marks for each element and example.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct element with example, up to 5.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent pupils, help keep order, and promote cleanliness. Accept organising activities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each function.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say no loudly, go to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: The president leads the national government of the whole country. The governor leads one county government.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: The patron is a teacher who guides and advises the pupil leaders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a teacher, 1 mark for guides the pupil leaders.
